summary: C-0006: Genuinely UNRESOLVED — (a) whether the brain changes are CAUSAL or epiphenomenal; (b) whether hypnotizability is a trait or a state-dependent capacity; (c) which specific mechanistic theory (cold control vs dissociated control vs SATH vs ability-based) is correct
content: CLAIM C-0006: Several load-bearing sub-questions remain genuinely unresolved per the 2024-2025 literature: (a) Causal vs epiphenomenal: Wagstaff's epiphenomenal hypothesis (brain changes are real but don't cause responsiveness) vs causal-state views is not decisively adjudicated — Dell/Lush ability models emphasize this gap ('no study has controlled all relevant non-hypnotic variables... post hoc ergo propter hoc'). (b) Trait vs state: alpha-peak variability (2024) appears post-induction (state-like) while arrhythmic EEG discriminates susceptibility at BASELINE (trait-like) — both coexist. (c) Mechanism plurality: cold control and dissociated control make OPPOSITE rTMS predictions (cold control: DLPFC disruption LOWERS response; dissociated control: RAISES it), and empirical TMS results are mixed (Dienes & Hutton supported; Coltheart et al. partially failed to replicate; Faerman et al. supported with personalized TMS). No single mechanism has won. SUPPORTS: the honest answer is 'contested on multiple axes', not 'one side won'.
